title: Telemetry Gateway Concordance: adaptive schema reconciliation and rollback signaling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a Telemetry Gateway Concordance service that performs adaptive schema reconciliation for incoming usage events, computes a compact event fingerprint, and emits rollback signals when a regression in shape fidelity or downstream mapping is detected. This is intended to reduce silent ingestion drift and reduce alert noise from strict reject/passthrough strategies. The service will sit in front of the primary ingestion pipeline and operate in three modes: observe-only (scoring), soft-accept (auto-coerce + metric tagging), and enforce (reject + telemetry).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Service ingests 10k events/s per pod in trial environment with <50ms p95 processing overhead. 2) Concordance scoring aligns with current schema registry baseline for 95% of event types in first-week rollouts. 3) Rollback signals are emitted to the rollout manager and appear on the console incident dashboard when score drops >15% for 10 minutes. 4) No customer-visible failures for soft-accept mode rollout across canary tenants.
design_decisions: - Use compact 128-bit fingerprint derived from event shape (field paths and primitive types) plus sampling of typical values. - Reconciliation runs a staged heuristic: exact-key match -> permissive coercion -> field-mapper with whitelist -> flag for manual mapping. - Maintain time-windowed concordance score per event-type and tenant to detect regressions. - Rollback signal is a signed event posted to the rollout service; retry+backoff for transient failures. - Persist minimal schema history in Bigtable for efficient lookups and join with telemetry metrics in BigQuery for reporting.
implementation_notes: - New microservice (concordance-gateway) in console-backend k8s namespace. - GRPC ingress from frontend collectors, HTTP API for manual inspection. - Streaming pipeline uses Kafka topic telemetry.inbound.precheck and writes annotated events to telemetry.inbound.postcheck. - Add feature flag gate in the console to toggle modes per tenant. - Metrics: concordance_score (gauge), fingerprint_count (counter), rollback_signal_emitted (counter), processing_latency_ms (histogram).
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy observe-only to staging for 2 weeks, collect baseline and tune heuristics. 2) Canary soft-accept for 5 low-risk tenants for 3 days. 3) Expand soft-accept to 25% traffic with monitoring dashboards and SLO alarms. 4) If stable, enable enforce mode for internal tenants first before enterprise customers. 5) Provide per-tenant opt-out and emergency kill-switch in console.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for fingerprint generation and reconciliation heuristics. - E2E tests with synthetic event corpus covering schema drift scenarios. - Load test using k6 to validate 10k events/s per pod. - Chaos tests to validate retry/backoff when rollout-service is unavailable. - Integration test linking to console dashboards and verifying rollback signal ingestion.
risks: - False positives in rollback detection could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; mitigated by dampening window and manual confirmation step for high-impact tenants. - Fingerprint collisions for polymorphic payloads; mitigate by adding sampled value entropy to fingerprint. - Performance overhead increasing end-to-end latency; mitigate with fast-path cache and approximate scoring for common types. - Operational complexity for Release Engineers and SREs during rollout; include runbook and on-call playbook.
